title: BDL Intermediate Circular No. 761: KYC Form for Currency Transactions and Exchange Operations
text:
Intermediate Circular No. 761
Addressed to Financial Institutions, Specialized Lending Entities (Comptoirs),
Exchange Institutions, and Electronic Payment Services Providers
Attached is a copy of Intermediate Decision No. 13815 of 4 May 2026, amending Basic
Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025 on the KYC Form for Cash Transactions and
Exchange Operations notified by Basic Circular No. 3 to Financial Institutions.
Beirut, 4 May 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
1

Intermediate Decision No. 13815
Amending Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025 on the
KYC Form for Cash Transactions and Exchange Operations
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, in particular Articles 70 and 174 thereof;
Pursuant to Law No. 133 of 26 October 1999 on the General Mission of the Banque du
Liban;
Pursuant to Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025 on the KYC Form for Cash
Transactions and Exchange Operations; and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, taken in its
meeting of 29 April 2026,
Decides the following:
Article 1: The title of Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025 shall be repealed
and replaced with: “KYC Form for Cash Transactions”.
Article 2: Articles 1 to 7 of Basic Decision No. 13769 of 14 November 2025, as well as
Announcement No. 975 of 10 February 2026, and all appendices attached to
both the Circular and the Announcement shall be repealed and replaced with the
following:
“Article 1: Definitions:
For the purposes of this Decision, the following terms shall have the meanings
hereunder assigned to them:
- Non-Banking Financial Institutions (NBFIs): financial institutions,
specialized lending entities (comptoirs), exchange institutions, and
Electronic Payment Services Providers regulated by the Banque du Liban.
- Cash Transactions: any transaction in which a cash amount equal to, or
above USD 1,000 is deposited, withdrawn, paid, or received by a natural
person or legal entity (e.g., E-money, electronic money transfer, lending,
currency exchange, and collection services).
2

Article 2: Scope of Implementation
In accordance with applicable regulations, the BDL directives, and AML/CFT
international standards, and with a view to prevent the misuse of the licensed financial
system in suspicious or high-risk operations, NBFIs are required to:
1. Collect, verify, record, and store systematically all information and data
related to customers and transactions.
2. Develop and implement effective policies and procedures in order to detect
unusual or suspicious transactions, particularly recurring transactions
suspected of being aimed at circumventing the designated threshold for cash
transactions.
Article 3: Monitoring of Transactions
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1. Apply a USD 1,000 threshold or its equivalent on a transactional basis.
2. Flag recurring transactions whose apparent aim is to circumvent this threshold,
and take the necessary measures to detect and address them.
3. Abide by the AML/CFT policies and procedures in place at the Institution, and
by the obligation to report suspicious transactions as per applicable
regulations.
Article 4: Forms RF1-A and RF1-B and their Completion
When adopting the two Forms for Cash Transactions, NBFIs are required to comply
with the following:
1. Complete Form RF1-A when carrying out any cash transaction equal to, or
above USD 1,000 or its equivalent. This Form shall be completed once by the
concerned customer, and updated periodically according to the customer's risk
category, provided that the update does not exceed five years for any
customer.
2. Complete Form RF1-B when carrying out any cash transaction equal to, or
above USD 1,000 or its equivalent, on a transactional basis, except for cash
withdrawals. Both Forms shall be retained for at least five years.
3. Forms RF1-A and RF1-B shall be signed physically by both the customer and
the Institution.
4. Forms RF1-A and RF1-B may be signed electronically by the customer who is
a natural person, as per the electronic signature conditions specified in both
Basic Decision No. 13790 of 9 January 2026 and Basic Decision No. 7548 of
30 March 2000, provided that the value of the cash transaction or the total
value of recurring transactions by the same customer at the concerned
institution does not exceed a monthly amount of USD 10,000.
Article 5: Identity Verification and Source of Funds
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1- Verify the identity of the customer for each cash transaction, and keep a copy
of a valid identification document bearing their photo.
2- Update the identification document upon expiry.
3- Identify the source of funds without requiring the customer to provide
supporting documentation, unless:
- The value of the cash transaction or the total value of recurring
transactions by the same customer at the concerned institution is equal to,
or above USD 10,000 or its equivalent, per month.
- There are suspicions regarding the cash transaction, or the nature of the
transaction is inconsistent with the information provided in Form RF1-A.
3

Article 6: Record-Keeping and Reporting
NBFIs are required to comply with the following:
1. Securely store all information and documents related to cash transactions
for at least five years.
2. Submit to the Banque du Liban, within two business days, daily reports (a
separate report for each day) via the email (fx-curr-rf1@bdl.gov.lb), as per
the attached Form (Daily Transactions Report) prepared in Excel format,
available at the following link: Click to download.
Article 7: Sanctions
Any person that violates the provisions of this Decision shall incur the administrative
sanctions specified in Article 208 of the Code of Money and Credit. The infringing
institution shall also incur daily delay penalties calculated in US dollars and fixed by
the Central Council. Furthermore, the violation of the provisions of this Decision
shall constitute an offense under Article 770 of the Penal Code, and the Banque du
Liban may pursue any infringing institution before the competent judicial authority.”
Article 3: This Decision shall come into force as of 30 June 2026.
Article 4: This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, 4 May 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
4
